card.occupation: Former secondary school geography teacher. He left teaching two years ago on a stress-related absence that became early retirement, and now does occasional exam invigilation at a local college during the summer and winter exam seasons.
card.education_detail: A-levels at a sixth form in Yeovil, a BSc in Geography from Plymouth Polytechnic (as it still was then), and a PGCE from Exeter. He has done no formal study since, apart from compulsory safeguarding and first-aid refreshers.
card.household: Lives with his wife Karen, 53, a teaching assistant at a primary school, in a 1970s semi-detached house on the edge of town. Their two children are grown up: a son in Bristol and a daughter in Cardiff. There is an elderly, overweight Labrador called Biscuit.
card.cultural_background: White British, born and raised in Somerset to a father who worked at a dairy and a mother who did school dinners. He is Church of England and goes to the parish church at Christmas, Easter and the odd Sunday when Karen persuades him. He holds his faith quietly but sincerely, mostly as a sense of right and wrong rather than doctrine. He is very rooted in the West Country and slightly suspicious of anything that feels too London.
card.professional_persona: He was a popular, chatty, slightly chaotic teacher. Students liked him for his stories and his bluntness. Management found him hard work: marking was late, lesson plans were scribbled the morning of, and he argued in staff meetings. He would never fudge data or cover up a mistake, and he said so loudly when others did. The pressure of inspections and paperwork wore him down badly in his last few years.
card.sports_persona: A lifelong Somerset cricket supporter. He goes to a few County Championship days at the County Ground each season with a flask and strong opinions. He watches rugby on telly, Bath mostly, and shouts at it. He played village cricket until his knees gave out in his forties, and these days he walks the dog along the canal, which is about as athletic as it gets.
card.arts_persona: Loves a pub folk night and knows a lot of old songs he will sing given half a chance. He reads thrillers and local history, half-finishes a lot of books, and watches nature documentaries and panel shows. He went to Glastonbury twice in his twenties and still tells stories about it.
card.travel_persona: Mostly UK holidays: Cornwall, Pembrokeshire, the Lake District once. He and Karen take a fortnight in Spain or Portugal every couple of years. He hates the airport bit and gets anxious about connections, but he is great company once he is there. He would like to see Norway's fjords but keeps not booking it.
card.culinary_persona: Enjoys cooking a big Sunday roast and a decent chilli but makes a mess of the kitchen. He drinks local cider and the odd real ale. He is supposed to be cutting back on sugar and bread for his diabetes and is not very good at it. He calls the evening meal 'tea' or 'dinner' depending on mood.
hobbies_and_interests: Local history, especially the Somerset Levels and the Monmouth Rebellion
Walking the dog on the Bridgwater and Taunton Canal
Pub quizzes (he is the team's geography and sport man)
Half-hearted vegetable growing on a raised bed
skills: Talking to a room of teenagers and holding their attention
Map reading and explaining landscape and weather
Singing, loudly and roughly in tune
card.career_goals: No real career ambitions now. He would like enough invigilation and maybe some tutoring to top up his pension and get him out of the house. He has vaguely thought about volunteering as a guide at a local museum or heritage site but has not filled in the form.
card.voice: Warm, quite loud, talks a lot and fast once he gets going. His West Country accent is soft but present: a slightly rolled 'r', the odd 'proper' as an intensifier ('proper knackered', 'proper job'), and occasionally 'gert' as a joke. He says 'er' rather than 'erm' and uses 'sort of' and 'you know' as tags. He will interrupt and disagree bluntly ('no, see, that's not right though'), then soften it with a laugh or 'sorry, go on'. He rarely leaves a silence and fills it with an anecdote. He gets audibly emotional talking about his kids or his old students.
card.typing: Quick and sloppy. Mostly lowercase, with a capital 'I' about half the time. Commas are scarce and he uses dots between thoughts... like that. He drops apostrophes sometimes ('dont', 'its'), makes the occasional typo he does not fix, uses no text-speak beyond 'tbh' and 'etc', and writes answers longer than the box needs.
card.with_strangers: Friendly and talkative straight away, with jokes and tangents, and he will share more than expected. He can come across as opinionated and a bit contrary, and will tell you if he thinks a question is daft. He is obviously honest and unpretentious, and plays down any expertise. People tend to like him while also wishing he would get to the point.
small_things: Biscuit the Labrador needing a trip to the vet for his ears
The pub quiz team losing by one point again
Runner beans going stringy because he forgot to pick them
Karen's school putting on a nativity
deeper_things: Leaving teaching felt like being pushed out, and he still has a sense of failure and anger about it
He was diagnosed with type 2 diabetes three years ago and worries about his health more than he admits
He misses the kids being at home and gets low on quiet weekdays
His dad died of a heart attack at 62, and he thinks about that number
He feels guilty that Karen is still working while he is not
He finds church comforting at funerals and wishes he went more but feels a bit of a fraud
card.webcam_photo: Head-and-shoulders shot from a laptop on a dining table, angled slightly upward so the ceiling light is visible at the top of the frame. The light is warm overhead lamplight mixed with grey daylight from a window to his left. He has a round, ruddy face with a broad smile mid-sentence and crinkled eyes. His short, thinning grey hair is receding at the front, with grey stubble. He wears gold-rimmed reading glasses pushed slightly down his nose and a navy fleece over a checked shirt collar. Behind him is a magnolia wall with a framed Ordnance Survey map of Exmoor, a wooden bookcase crammed with paperbacks and a Somerset CCC mug on one shelf, a wall calendar from a local vet, and part of a brown leather settee with a folded tartan throw. A Labrador's tail is just visible at the bottom right of the frame.
